$comment: Machine-readable migration state, one entry per domain area. Read by tests/parity/ownership-guard.mjs and, from session 2 onward, by site/erp-bridge.js. Update this file in the SAME commit that changes an area's owner — never lag behind the code.

owner.engine: Fully implemented in site/erp-engine.js today; erp.html reads/writes it directly or via ErpBridge pass-through.
owner.factory: Implemented as a packages/ capability, reached through site/erp-bridge.js. erp-engine.js may still hold a shrinking legacy copy during transition; erp.html must not call it directly once an area is 'factory'.
owner.unbuilt: No implementation anywhere yet (neither erp-engine.js nor packages/). Net-new capability work.

$schema.specSection: Section number in Requirements/20260731_REQUERMIENTOS BÁSICO CANEI.docx this area corresponds to.
$schema.engineSection: The section-divider comment in site/erp-engine.js that implements this area today, or null if unbuilt.
$schema.plannedSession: The session number (see the plan) expected to move this area to its next owner state.

budgets-versions.note: Session 9 built the three-zone constructor of §3.3 (chapter/line tree, editable grid, live totals panel) but deliberately did NOT move this area: the constructor is a view, and every figure it shows — line amounts, chapter subtotals, base, tax, withholding, total, margin, the value of the lines still pending a price — is asked of erp.budgetTotals(), the same function the emitted document uses. That is what makes the panel genuinely live rather than an optimistic copy that drifts from the document by a cent. The grid edits through erp.editLine(), which goes through _editableVersion, so a frozen, issued or accepted version refuses the edit. plannedSession is null because there is no pending move: totals and versioning are correct where they are, and a capability would be a rewrite for its own sake.

budget-graphic-annex.note: Owned by @repo/capability-docs (src/annex.ts) and reached only through site/erp-bridge.js (ErpBridge.docs.annex). The capability decides the whole layout — grouping and ordering by chapter then line number, the correlative numbering when a line has several pictures, the pagination at N per page, and which rows carry the discreet reference mark — from a list of images it is handed; it never touches bytes and never decides eligibility. The engine keeps what is genuinely its own: the image records on a line, the per-budget switch, and the fact that issuing a version snapshots the annex settings onto it so a sent document can always be reproduced. Bytes live in the blob store under storageKey (session 3's rule: binary never enters the state blob), compressed by the host before they are stored. Internal-only images are dropped at the document boundary by renderBudgetDoc, alongside cost and margin — a value that never enters the customer document cannot leak out of one.

projects.note: Session 10a built the persistent project selector and the fixed header of §4 (one context for every subsection, so two screens can never show different jobs at once) and added progress by executed quantity, per-chapter progress, committed cost per chapter and the stored forecast overrides. The area stays engine on purpose: the frozen baselines, the numbering, the acceptance-to-project inheritance and the cost ledger are all correct where they are, and the two derivations that genuinely did not exist — the plan from the budget, and cost at completion — went to capabilities instead. Moving the rest would be a rewrite for its own sake.

project-economics.note: Cost at completion is owned by @repo/capability-projects (src/forecast.ts) and reached through ErpBridge.projects.forecast. The split is deliberate and is the whole point of the area: erp-engine.js keeps reporting what HAS happened — the frozen baseline, committed and actual cost, approved change orders, chapter progress — and the capability answers what it IMPLIES. "Spent 40 of a 100 budget" reads as comfortable and says nothing; "spent 40 to get a quarter of the way, so heading for 160" is the sentence somebody can act on, and it did not exist anywhere before. A forecast never comes in below what is already spent or committed, a chapter with nothing booked keeps its budget whatever its progress says (finished-with-no-bill means the bill has not arrived, not that the work was free), and a human override is stored with a required reason and reported ALONGSIDE the calculation rather than replacing it. Nothing moved out of the engine for this to be true.

scheduling-gantt.note: Owned by @repo/capability-scheduling and reached only through ErpBridge.scheduling.plans. Session 6 gave it the calendar, CPM and baselines; session 10a added the three things §4.3 asks for around them: the real derivation from the accepted budget (chapters and lines in, durations from quantity divided by the vertical pack's daily output, dependencies chained, re-derivable without losing what the site recorded), the progress curve, and the risk report. Two properties are load-bearing. Derived task ids come from the caller's own references rather than a generator, so re-deriving after a quote change is a merge and not a reset. And the actual-progress curve is drawn from an append-only progress log, never from today's percentages: dates and the critical path recompute from the network at any time, but how much was done by the end of March is only knowable if somebody wrote it down in March.

extraction-ocr.note: Session 7 built the reading half: @repo/capability-extraction turns recognised text into candidate fields with confidence, provenance and arithmetic checks, and @repo/pack-jurisdiction-es-es supplies the profile behind the extraction-profile@1 port (number and date notation, NIF/CIF/NIE and IBAN check characters, the words each field is announced by, the rates in force on a date). Still 'unbuilt' here because no screen reaches it: session 8 adds the camera, the recognition adapter and the validation screen, and flips this. Nothing is ever auto-confirmed — CAP-04 is enforced by the capability's type, which always reports confirmed:false.

three-panel-shell.note: Built in session 4, but purely in the view layer of site/erp.html — sections, subsections, the global bar and hash routing. engineSection is null because there is no business rule here to own: the shell reads counts and alerts through the same engine calls the views already use. Recorded as 'engine' rather than 'unbuilt' because it exists and is in use; there is no owner value for 'view-only'.

task-status-summary.note: First area served by the capability layer. Task counts by status are computed by @repo/capability-scheduling via site/erp-bridge.js, not by ad-hoc filtering in the view. The underlying task records are still owned by erp-engine.js (see alerts-tasks-control-tower) — only this derivation moved, which is what made it safe to land first.
